Pros:

1. It's simple and pretty straight forward
2. You never (mostly) are left in the dark about what to do next
3. You can be a "real" Hacker for once
4. Simple and understandable UI
5. Learn some Linux commands
6. Great Storyline
7. The atmosphere and tense you get while hacking
8. A lot of hidden ingame stuff
9. The DLC "Labyrinths"

Neutral:

1. I can imagine that the music is not for everyone
2. Way too simple and straight forward compared to Uplink
3. Limited Options (while in Uplink you can hack Banks to get money or even give it to someone else, destory/save lives by manipulating police entries and such)
4. Missing does insane minigames, from Uplink, to crack a Lan and the option to build your own computersetup 

In-Depth Review:

I don't know if people still know that gem of a game called "Uplink". It's from the Year 2001 and was one of the best science fiction games back then (still is, but didnt aged very well). Hacknet is just a modern version of "Uplink". But it's extremly simplified compared to it, which have it's pros and it's cons of being so ofc. While Hacknet never reaches that incredible Depth Uplink offered, it's still have a lot of great moments itself, mostly because of a good storyline you can follow.

Hacknet is basically a pure text-based game in a science fiction setting. You are hacking computers, databases and other stuff 100% of the time. You wont do anything else. Don't except to buy your own computerparts, or anything like that. Playtime is around 10-20 hours and more if you have the DLC. 

The game is pretty easy and very straight forward. I have the feeling the game is holding your hands for a bit too long. But when it finally let you loose, oh boy, the felling of power and control is just awesome. There so many secrets to discover and little hidden stuff to look out for, it keeps you occupied for a few hours. And the music (it varies, but sometimes it's psytrance-like music and you get the felling you are on a Goa-Party) is pushing you all the time. You really fell like a "Supa Hacka" at times.

If you like the basegame, check out the DLC "Labyrinths" as well, because it lets you loose right from the start. It offers a own storyline to follow, new features, executables and Themes. 

Overall Hacknet and it's DLC, surely is worth the money if you like text-based adventures, want to learn/relearn a few basic Linux/Dos commands on the way, looking for a new Uplink for years (like myself), or just want to be a "Supa Hacka" for once.

Don't let the terminal screen and techno-nonsense trick you—Hacknet is a deceptively simple game to play. You use a series of commands to "hack" into terminals both as a contract hacker and on a mission, one to find the reason for a fellow hacker's untimely death.

It's in large part due to its phenomenal soundtrack and well-realised interface, but no game this year has made me feel like more of a badass than Hacknet. Its presentation is executed so well that every action you take feels like you've been doing them for years, like hacking into networks is just child's play.

It plays very much like a puzzle-adventure game, so if something like that is up your alley, it's really worth checking out.

Also, it's worth playing to see the final hacking sequence alone.

Hacknet is an excellent hacker "simulator". I say "simulator" because the technical details are simplified in this game. But Hacknet simplifies things just enough to make it an accessible game almost for everybody. The main focus of the game is on the atmosphere. And all the elements of the atmosphere are great in this game: the interface, the music, the interactions with other hackers and the process of digging in someone's else private information.
Most of the game you are doing various hacking mission which usually require you to find a certain information on a server. A mission takes about 5-15 minutes to complete, so you can play this game in short sessions.
You don't need any prior knowledge in hacking/programming/networking to play this game, but I think you'll like this game only if you have interest in this kind of things. And of course you have to read a lot in this game.

Had this on my wish list for a long time and finally purchased it. Firstly, this game is not for everyone. Even if you THINK you would find it fun to play a hacking game, you will become frustrated quick when you realize it takes some work to get it right. You will be given a quick introduction, some references to read (I recommend reading them) and then tested to solve problems like your own terminal being hacked. The community is helpful, but don't expect to have your hand held with "How to do it" advice. Expect only nudges to point you in the right direction. 

Thus far, the game has been intense for me and I look forward to more self induced stress lol. There is something giddy about being where your not supposed to be. Then getting out before anyone knows you where there, or running out before you get caught. I like the feel of the terminal interface and the requirement that you need to be (or willing to be) comfortable with a command prompt. I have not encountered any bugs as of yet and the game is very stable on my Win10 system. The only gripe I have is some of the documentation on the in game archive servers is hard to read do to grammar/typos. Like it was translated to English from some other language. This was fine and added to the realism when reading IRC logs and stuff but detracted from my experience when I was trying to learn a little more.

I'm only 6 hrs in, as of this writing, but I am hooked enough to know that I would recommend HackNet.

Fun little hacking game. 

It has a few flaws: Firstly, notes taking up RAM, let alone a lot of RAM. I sort of get what the devs were going for here, but all it does is encourage the player to pull  up a notepad on their second monitor, especially in the endgame when you need to juggle passwords and IP addresses for upwards of a dozen machines. It's a cool concept but its insanely cluttered and unusable, to the point where the DLC gives you a way to sort it, so the devs know its a problem. but you just have to deal with it until you beat the dlc (intended to be played late in the main story)

Beyond those flaws though, it's a very good little hacking game. The terminal setup is cool, the story is surprisingly compelling, and it's got a neat series of puzzles that are very intuitive, even for me as someone without a background in cyber security. Recommended, just, take your own notes.

Fantastic game. Beat it a while ago, but I figured I'd write a review anyway

Graphics are on point. It was very easy to get used to the interface, but I remember being a bit overwhelmed at the start. The semi-tutorial takes you through the process of the gameplay very nicely, so it's an overall smooth start.

The gameplay is fantastic. It does get a bit stale at one point in the game, and it gets a bit cryptic in some task descriptions, so I admit to having to look up a walkthrough every now and then. The puzzles are quite a lot of fun, and don't feel very repetitive, even if you get used to the generally pretty generic rhythm of the game.

There's a bit of missing suspense and a lack of clear enemies makes it a bit difficult to feel pressure when playing the game, but every now and then, a timer comes up, and it gets very dramatic, which elevates the gameplay a bit.

I loved playing it despite the small flaws. The gameplay is suprisingly riveting despite what might seem like a very simplistic set of controls. There are also tons of easter eggs hidden in the files you hack into, and reading them kinda relieves the seriousness of the game a bit, and makes room for some comedic moments

There were so many things that were beautiful about this game, and I admittedly got addicted to this game. It'll probably be a game that I'll often pick back up and play over and over again in the future, and I certainly don't have any complaints in that regard. 

It may be off limits to people who are easily confused or who tend to give up on things quickly once they become overwhelmed with new information, but otherwise, this game is easily worth over $40. It's $10. Just get it.

review_text_raw:
So I just finished the game.To be honest, I'm not what to think.
First of all, I quite impressed with the amount of detail that was put into it.
On the other hand, it has a lot of missed opportunities when it come to writing, UI-Design and some mechanics.
The (mostly) reallistic terminal commands really help the [b]immersion[/b].

And that's in my opinion the main selling point of this game. 
When sitting in a dark room; late at night; typing as fast as I could to avoid being traced;
That really had me at the edge of my seat...  So recommend everyone remotely interested in
real life hacking to give it a look. It's well worth your attention.

Although, I'm not quite sure if it was worth all the time I put into it. ([spoiler]-Clock.exe-[/spoiler])
The storyline is nothing groundbreaking and the writing tends to be dodgy at times. But what really made me stop playing for a while before I finished it: The missions get really repetitive. Mostly, because the different .exe exploits/scripts/hacks don't differ mechanically. It's just type whichever you see fit and wait for it to finish. Which is in my opinion the games biggest flaw. (I'm not sure I'm missing the point because it's supposed to reallistic, but after all, this is a game.)

Which is truly a shame, because these last few missions are really fun.
So if you can keep up the grind, go get and finish this.

Oh, and, I really wish to see a "Hacknet 2".
